statements.proposition: The change introduces no breaking changes and is fully backwards compatible.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: No public name was removed, renamed or re-signatured (diff is an import-time try/except plus an extras entry), which supports the claim. But the import now globally calls truststore.inject_into_ssl() whenever truststore is installed, which changes SSL trust behaviour for any program importing lastversion; whether that counts as breaking is not settleable by a concrete check.
evidence: gh api pulls/189/files: only setup.py (+1) and src/lastversion/__init__.py (+8) modified
__init__.py patch adds try: import truststore; truststore.inject_into_ssl() except ImportError: pass before the existing imports; __all__ unchanged

statements.label: TRUE
statements.note: Repo configures flake8 (setup.cfg: select=C,E,F,W,B,B950; CI runs flake8 with --select=E9,F63,F7,F82 blocking, plus an --exit-zero full run). On the two changed files, the CI blocking command and the full run with CI's max-line-length=127/complexity=10 are clean. With setup.cfg defaults flake8 reports 3 B950 line-length findings in setup.py (lines 24, 25, 105), which are on lines the PR did not touch and exist at the base too. Labelled by CI configuration; flake8-bugbear was installed unpinned (latest).
